short: Server health and security, with the fix for every problem
long:
Kiyesi checks a Linux server's health and security and prints each problem
in one sentence with the command that fixes it. The scan and the agent only
read: they never change a file, a setting or a container. Only sudo kiyesi fix,
which you run and answer yourself, makes a change, and most can be undone.

Alone, kiyesi shows what needs you now and the next command to run.
example:
kiyesi              what needs you now, and the next command
  sudo kiyesi scan    this server's report; nothing leaves it

short: Run as the background service: scan and send results (started by kiyesi connect)
long:
Runs a scan now and every 15 minutes, says the server is alive every minute
(less often on the free plan, as the service asks),
and sends both to the service. Results that cannot be sent wait on disk and
are sent later. It is normally started by the system service.
example:
sudo systemctl status kiyesi
  KIYESI_API=https://api.kiyesi.dev KIYESI_TOKEN=ksv_... kiyesi agent --container

short: Fix what Kiyesi can fix on this server, after you say yes (needs sudo)
long:
Lists the findings Kiyesi can fix for you, says in plain words what each fix
changes, and asks. After you say yes it makes the changes, checks the server
again and shows the new grade. Every change that can be undone is kept:
kiyesi fix undo lists them. Before a fix changes a file it saves it, and a fix
that fails halfway is put back at once. Three cannot be undone: installing
updates (updates), renewing certificates (certificates) and removing unused
Docker images and build cache (docker-cleanup).

Only you run this, at this server's terminal. The agent's service never runs
it, and the dashboard cannot ask for it. To forbid it on a server, set
fix: off in /etc/kiyesi/config.yaml. Names: certificates, docker-cleanup, firewall, login-protection, secret-files, ssh-password, ssh-root, updates.
example:
sudo kiyesi fix                 the list, then asks
  sudo kiyesi fix ssh-password    one fix
  sudo kiyesi fix --dry-run       only show what it would change
  sudo kiyesi fix undo            what can be undone

undone: installing updates (updates), renewing certificates (certificates)
and removing unused Docker images and build cache (docker-cleanup).
example:

short: Leave the team these commands are for
long:
Your open work goes back to Unassigned, and you need a new invite to come back.
A team's only owner makes someone else an owner first.

short: Choose which of your teams commands are for
long:
Someone in several teams chooses one; commands then show only that team.
Without a name, lists your teams and which one is in use.
example:
kiyesi team use
  kiyesi team use Globex

short: One request from the browser to the database, by its ID
long:
Shows one request as a row of steps, each with the time it took and how
that is known, where most of the time went, and its log lines.

flags.usage: print the result as JSON, for scripts

short: Slow or failed requests, and where their time went
long:
Lists requests followed by their ID from the browser through the web server
and the backend to the database, newest first: the slow (a second or more)
or failed ones, or all with --all. Open one with: kiyesi trace <id>

flags.name: all

flags.usage: print the result as JSON, for scripts

flags.usage: a request ID, or an address such as /api/orders

flags.name: since
flags.usage: how far back: 1h, 24h or 7d

short: Remove the agent and its files from this server
long:
Stops and removes the kiyesi service, the server token and settings in
/etc/kiyesi, the results waiting in /var/lib/kiyesi, and the kiyesi program.
What the server already sent stays in the dashboard: there, disconnect the
server to keep it until it expires, or delete it to erase it.

Changes made by kiyesi fix stay on the server, but their undo records go
with /var/lib/kiyesi, so kiyesi can no longer put them back. To put one back
first: sudo kiyesi fix undo

flags.name: keep-program
flags.usage: remove the service and its files but keep the kiyesi program, for one-off scans

flags.name: yes
flags.usage: do not ask first

short: Install the newest kiyesi, after checking its signature
long:
Downloads the newest release from get.kiyesi.dev, checks its signature with
the release key built into this program and the file's checksum, then
replaces this program in one step and restarts the agent if it runs.
Nothing is changed if any check fails. Updates never happen by themselves.

flags.name: check
flags.usage: only say whether a newer version is out
